question: A can lay railway track between two given stations in 21 days and B can do the same job in 16 days. With the help of C, they did the job in 2 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 21, 16, and 2 = 336 units.

Efficiency of A = 336 ÷ 21 = 16, Efficiency of B = 336 ÷ 16 = 21.

Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 336 ÷ 2 = 168.

Efficiency of C = 168 − (16 + 21) = 131 units/day.

Time taken by C = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C = 336 ÷ 131 = 2 ⁷⁴/₁₃₁ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ⁷⁴/₁₃₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 21 days

Time taken by B = 16 days

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 2 days

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

**Calculation:**

⇒ Efficiency of A = 16 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 21 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 168 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Total efficiency − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 168 − (16 + 21) = 168 − 37 = 131 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 336 ÷ 131 = 2 ⁷⁴/₁₃₁ days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ⁷⁴/₁₃₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

Works exactly like Time & Work, but filling pipes have positive efficiency and emptying pipes have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of work done. If time is constant, wages are distributed in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When persons work one by one on alternate days, calculate the total work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and multiply to approach the total work target.
